guideTitle: The Best CPU Stands for Carpet: Clearance and Stability
metaDescription: On carpet, a PC tower needs lifting clear of the pile. We compared six stands, from low rolling bases to a two-tier cart, on clearance, fit, rails and extras.
introParagraphs: A desktop tower sitting directly on carpet can draw fibers and dust into bottom intakes and can be awkward to move. A stand lifts it clear of the pile and gives it a flat, stable base.

The main choice is height: low rolling stands lift the tower an inch or two, enough for most carpet, while a tall cart like the ZIIWIND lifts it well clear and adds storage and charging. Fit matters too; measure your case's width and depth.
Most of these were under $25 at the time of writing. Our comparison is based on published specifications, not hands-on testing; few listings state a weight capacity.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-1.summary: A metal stand adjusting from 7.87 to 10.23 inches wide, 16.9 inches long, with side rails and wheels.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-1.description:
The Hovadova is the simple, low-cost choice: a metal stand whose width adjusts from 7.87 to 10.23 inches, 16.9 inches long, with protective rails on both sides, a ventilated base and wheels.

Its 16.9-inch length is shorter than some stands here, so check it against a deeper full-tower case.
cons: Capacity not stated in the summary
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-1.bestFor: Standard mid-tower cases on a budget.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-1.skipIf: Your case is wide; the BYMECOST adjusts to 11.81 inches.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-2.summary: YOSE's basic computer tower stand, the lowest-priced option here.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-2.description:
The YOSE stand was the least expensive option here at the time of writing, at under $15.

Its listing summary gives no specifications, so check dimensions, adjustment range and whether it has wheels on the product page before buying.
cons: No specifications in the listing summary
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-2.bestFor: A basic riser when price is the main concern.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-2.skipIf: You want listed specs; the BYMECOST states its range for about $1 more.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-3.summary: A width-adjustable stand that lifts the PC 1.75 inches, designed for carpet.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-3.description:
This stand raises the tower 1.75 inches off the floor, enough to clear carpet pile, with an adjustable width for most cases and free-rolling wheels.

The brand isn't named, and locking and capacity aren't stated in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-3.bestFor: Clearing carpet pile under a standard tower.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-3.skipIf: You want more clearance; the ZIIWIND cart lifts the tower much higher.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-4.summary: An adjustable rolling stand with side rails and four 360-degree wheels.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-4.description:
This stand covers the basics: side rails to keep the case from slipping off and four 360-degree wheels so you can roll the tower out to clean.

The listing summary doesn't give its width range or dimensions, so check them against your case before buying.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-4.bestFor: A basic rolling platform for a standard case.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-4.skipIf: You want stated dimensions; the Hovadova lists its range.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-5.summary: A 2-tier, 16.9 x 11.4-inch PC cart adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches tall, with a charging station.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-5.description:
The ZIIWIND is a two-tier PC cart rather than a low stand: 16.9 x 11.4 inches, with height adjustable from 19.7 to 31.5 inches, and a built-in charging station for your devices.

Lifting the tower well above the carpet keeps it clear of the pile. It was the most expensive option here at the time of writing and takes more space than a low stand.
pros: Lifts tower well clear of carpet
cons: Wheel details not stated in summary
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-5.bestFor: A tower cart that doubles as a charging spot.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-5.skipIf: You only want the tower off the carpet; a low stand costs far less.

best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-6.summary: BYMECOST's ventilated stand adjusting 7.87 to 11.81 inches wide, 15.75 inches long.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-6.description:
The BYMECOST fits wider cases than the Hovadova, adjusting from 7.87 to 11.81 inches wide with a 15.75-inch length, and has a ventilated base, at under $15 at the time of writing.

Its 15.75-inch length is on the short side for deep full towers, and wheel and lock details aren't in the listing summary.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-6.bestFor: Wider cases on carpet for little money.
best-cpu-stands-for-carpet-6.skipIf: Your case is long; a longer stand avoids overhang.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Check lift height where listed (1.75 inches on the carpet stand); thick carpet needs more.
Widths here range up to 11.81 inches (BYMECOST); lengths from 15.75 to 16.9 inches on low stands.
Side rails help keep the case steady when rolling over carpet.
Most listings don't state one; check before loading a heavy tower.

faq.q: Why use a stand on carpet?
faq.a: It lifts the tower clear of the pile, which can help keep fibers away from intakes and makes it easier to move.
Enough to clear the pile; thick carpet needs more clearance than low-pile office carpet.
They can, though larger casters roll more easily on thick pile.
Compare your case's width and depth with the stand's range.

faq.q: How much weight can they hold?
faq.a: Most listings don't state a capacity; check before buying for a heavy tower.

bottomLine: For most towers on carpet, the Hovadova is a low-cost stand with rails, and the BYMECOST fits wider cases. The dedicated carpet stand states a 1.75-inch lift.
If you want the tower well clear of the floor plus storage and charging, the ZIIWIND cart is the step up.
